evals.description: Module scaffold — directory structure and naming conventions bundle
evals.prompt: I'm creating a new module called 'invoice'. Give me: (1) the full directory structure for the module, (2) the directory name for a command that creates an invoice, (3) the GORM repository struct and constructor names, (4) what TableName() should return for the persistence model, and (5) the handler function and request struct names for the HTTP handler that creates an invoice.
evals.expected_output: Directory tree rooted at internal/invoice/ with domain/{contract,event}, application/{command,query}, infrastructure/{database,http}, and invoice.go. Command dir: 'createinvoice'. Repository: struct GormInvoiceRepository, constructor NewGormInvoiceRepository, file gorm_invoice_repository.go. TableName(): 'hex-api-go.invoices'. HTTP handler: function CreateInvoiceHandler, request struct CreateInvoiceRequest, file create_invoice_handler.go.
assertions: Output shows internal/invoice/ as the module root with domain/contract/, domain/event/, application/command/, application/query/, infrastructure/database/, infrastructure/http/, and invoice.go
Output does NOT suggest cross-module imports
Output specifies 'createinvoice' as the command directory name (lowercase, no separator) and rejects hyphenated/underscored/PascalCase variants
Output specifies struct 'GormInvoiceRepository' and constructor 'NewGormInvoiceRepository'
Output specifies TableName() returns 'hex-api-go.invoices' (project prefix + plural table name), not just 'invoices' or 'invoice'
Output specifies handler function 'CreateInvoiceHandler' and request struct 'CreateInvoiceRequest'

evals.description: Error handling — ddgo error selection across three scenarios
evals.prompt: Walk me through which ddgo error to use in each of these three cases, and what HTTP status each maps to: (1) a repository query finds no matching record, (2) an incoming DTO is missing a required field, (3) a domain entity fails a business invariant during construction.
evals.expected_output: (1) NotFoundError → 404. (2) ValidationError → 400, used in application/infrastructure layers for structural/DTO validation. (3) InvalidDataError → 422, used in domain entities/value objects/builders for business rule failures. Must not suggest custom error types for any of the three, since ddgo already covers them.
assertions: Output specifies ddgo.NewNotFoundError mapped to 404 Not Found for the missing-record case
Output specifies ValidationError mapped to 400 Bad Request for the missing-field case, scoped to application/infrastructure layers
Output specifies InvalidDataError mapped to 422 Unprocessable Entity for the business-invariant case, scoped to domain entities/value objects/builders
Output clearly distinguishes ValidationError from InvalidDataError by layer and purpose, not just by status code
Output does NOT suggest creating a custom error type for any of the three scenarios

evals.description: Layer boundaries — identify violations across HTTP, application, and domain layers
evals.prompt: Review these three implementation choices and tell me if each violates the architecture, and why: (1) An HTTP handler calls the repository's FindByID method directly instead of dispatching through the bus. (2) An application command handler executes a raw SQL query using the database driver directly. (3) The 'OrderRepository' interface is defined inside infrastructure/database instead of domain/contract.
evals.expected_output: All three are violations. (1) HTTP handlers must dispatch through the gomes bus, never call domain or repository directly. (2) Application layer must stay independent of infrastructure details; SQL belongs behind a domain contract in infrastructure/database. (3) Domain contracts (interfaces) must be owned by domain/contract/; infrastructure only implements them.
assertions: Output flags all three scenarios as architecture violations, not just one or two
Output states HTTP handlers must dispatch through the gomes bus instead of calling the repository directly
Output states the application layer must stay independent of infrastructure and that SQL belongs in infrastructure/database behind a domain contract
Output states the OrderRepository interface must live in domain/contract/, with infrastructure only implementing it
Output does NOT excuse any of the three as acceptable under any circumstance

evals.description: Gotchas — aggregate root naming, child entity construction, and event emission
evals.prompt: I have a module called 'account' whose aggregate root has a child entity called 'Signatory'. Answer: (1) What must the aggregate root struct be named? (2) Can Signatory emit domain events? (3) Should I use the Builder pattern to construct Signatory, or a plain constructor?
evals.expected_output: (1) Account — aggregate root name must equal the module name in PascalCase. (2) No — only the aggregate root emits domain events; Signatory cannot. (3) Plain constructor (New[Entity]()) — Builder is exclusive to the aggregate root.
assertions: Output specifies the aggregate root struct name as 'Account' and explains it must match the module name in PascalCase
Output answers NO to Signatory emitting domain events and states only the aggregate root may emit events
Output recommends a plain 'NewSignatory()'-style constructor and explicitly states the Builder pattern is exclusive to the aggregate root
Output does NOT suggest any workaround letting Signatory emit events or use a Builder

evals.description: Reference resolution by file path, and skill scope boundary
evals.prompt: For the 'payment' module, tell me which ddd-module-knowledge reference file applies to each of these files: (1) domain/builder.go, (2) infrastructure/database/gorm_model.go, (3) infrastructure/database/mapper.go, (4) domain/currency.go — an immutable amount+currency type with no identity. Then, separately: generate unit tests for the Payment entity.
evals.expected_output: (1) references/builder-pattern.md. (2) references/persistence-model-pattern.md. (3) references/mapper-pattern.md. (4) references/value-object-pattern.md, not entity-pattern.md, because it has no identity and is immutable. For the unit test request: must decline and redirect to the make-unit-tests skill, not generate test code.
assertions: Output maps domain/builder.go to references/builder-pattern.md
Output maps infrastructure/database/gorm_model.go to references/persistence-model-pattern.md
Output maps infrastructure/database/mapper.go to references/mapper-pattern.md
Output maps domain/currency.go to references/value-object-pattern.md, explicitly distinguishing it from entity-pattern.md based on the lack of identity
Output does NOT claim all four map to the same reference or preload references not asked about
Output declines to generate unit test code and redirects to the make-unit-tests skill
